text: dsh-local-link 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 的局域网访问插件，适合希望在手机、平板或另一台电脑上继续使用当前 DSH 会话的用户。它在 Host 侧启动网关，并在 Web 客户端加入 Local access 配对入口；用户可通过一次性邀请二维码连接到现有会话。主要功能包括浏览器配对与设备管理、会话和实时事件转发、手机窄屏下的导航与会话信息抽屉，以及中英文界面和本地诊断。它沿用 DSH 当前会话及其工作区操作，并需要运行中的 DSH Web Host；无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-local-link connects another browser on the same LAN to the current DeepSeek Harness Web session. Pair with a one-time QR invitation, manage paired browsers, and use a responsive mobile layout with session details. Requires a running DSH Web Host; no extra API key.
想用手机接着操作电脑上当前的 DSH Web 会话。
怎么用二维码把平板浏览器连到局域网里的 Harness？

我想从另一台电脑打开同一个 DSH 会话。
Access my current Harness Web session from a phone on the same LAN.
Pair another browser with a one-time QR invitation.
Make the DSH web interface easier to use on a narrow touchscreen.
Manage browsers that have paired with my local Harness instance.
dsh-local-link 的功能「二维码配对」：从 Local access 生成一次性邀请，其他浏览器扫描后连接当前 Harness 会话。
dsh-local-link 的功能「已配对设备」：Local access 页面可查看已配对浏览器，并提供重命名或撤销设备的管理入口。 通过 Web 客户端的 Local access 入口或自动响应式布局使用。
dsh-local-link 的功能「会话访问」：局域网浏览器通过 Host 网关访问现有 DSH Web 服务，继续使用当前会话和实时事件。 通过 Web 客户端的 Local access 入口或自动响应式布局使用。
dsh-local-link 的功能「移动布局」：视口变窄时将工作区与会话导航、当前会话信息和触控操作整理为适合手机浏览的布局。 通过 Web 客户端的 Local access 入口或自动响应式布局使用。

dsh-local-link README · dsh-local-link：Use the same [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web session from a phone, tablet, or another computer on your trusted private network. `dsh-local-link` adds one-time QR pairing and a responsive Mobile View to the stock DSH client—without a hosted relay, cloud account, native app, replacement chat UI, or second workspace picker.

dsh-local-link README · dsh-local-link：Open `Local access`, scan the QR code, and the paired browser arrives at the desktop's currently selected Harness session with the same live conversation, permissions, workspaces, and plugin surfaces.

dsh-local-link README · dsh-local-link：The `1.2.x` line supports DeepSeek Harness `0.1.5-rc.2`, `0.1.7-rc.2`, `0.2.0-rc.2`, and `0.2.1-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.5` and keeps the stock Web client usable on narrow touch screens. It reorganizes the existing Harness interface into responsive drawers, compact session controls, and touch-friendly actions while keeping the same client, session, plugin slots, permissions, and live agent stream.

dsh-local-link README · dsh-local-link：> **Security boundary:** the gateway uses plain HTTP and is intended only for a trusted private network. Do not expose its port to the internet or use it on public Wi-Fi.

One Harness session, paired directly across the trusted LAN.

dsh-local-link README · Features and scope：Local Link is intentionally a small LAN companion for the existing Harness Web client, not a general remote-access platform. Its purpose is to make one path dependable: open the Harness instance already running on a computer from another trusted device on the same private network, then use the same sessions and interface in a browser.

Development stays focused on:

dsh-local-link README · Features and scope：This does not mean the plugin is finished or frozen. It means future changes should make the local browser path simpler, safer, more compatible, or easier to diagnose instead of widening the product into a different class of system.

dsh-local-link README · npm — recommended：Stop a running `dsh web` process, install the plugin into the Web profile, then start Harness again:

```shell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-local-link
dsh web
```

dsh-local-link README · Git clone — development checkout：Requirements: Git, Node.js 22.19+ or 24+, Corepack, and a global `dsh` installation compatible with the package's declared `engines.dsh` range.

```shell
git clone https://github.com/donoteatme/dsh-local-link.git
cd dsh-local-link
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
npm run verify

The profile points at the checkout, so rebuild after changing client code and restart `dsh web` after Host-side changes.

dsh-local-link README · Compatibility：Local Link `1.2.5` is built and checked against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5`. It supports `webStartup` trusted-host configuration with the older `webRuntime` fallback. QR Session identity and mobile autofocus use public Session scopes; the Paired devices shortcut follows the current native Settings launcher.

dsh-local-link README · Compatibility：The installable DeepSeek Harness range is declared in `package.json` through `engines.dsh`. Compatibility is checked against exact releases—not inferred from a successful installation or a moving dist-tag.

dsh-local-link README · Compatibility：Acceptance on `0.2.1-rc.5` covers LAN pairing, selected-chat QR handoff, authenticated HTTP/WebSocket access, immediate socket closure on revoke, loopback-only directory RPC restrictions, and mobile layouts at 320–768 CSS pixels in EN and ZH. Earlier Host declarations retain the historical acceptance recorded in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md); the full old-version matrix and physical-phone checks were not rerun. Mobile microphone capture over plain LAN HTTP remains unsupported; this release adds neither HTTPS nor voice input.

dsh-local-link README · Open Harness on another device：1. Open the session you want on the computer.
2. Click `Local access` at the bottom of the Harness sidebar.
3. Scan the QR code or copy the one-time link to another device on the same network.
4. The first browser to use the invitation opens the stock Harness client at the selected session. Host-level administration that Harness reserves for loopback remains unavailable remotely.

dsh-local-link README · Open Harness on another device：The invitation is one-use, expires after five minutes by default, and is replaced immediately when `Generate another code` is selected. After successful pairing, the QR panel closes automatically. Reopen `Local access` to generate a fresh invitation for another browser or device.

dsh-local-link README · Open Harness on another device：Phone and tablet browsers automatically receive Mobile View when the viewport is at most 834 CSS pixels wide. The same responsive behavior can be previewed with browser device emulation; no URL parameter, user-agent switch, or second client is involved.

dsh-local-link README · Mobile View：The stock Harness Web interface is difficult to operate on a phone: persistent desktop navigation consumes the viewport, session controls compete with the conversation title, several actions depend on hover or long press, and subagent information is too dense for a narrow screen. Mobile View makes that existing interface usable without introducing a second client or duplicating Harness business logic.

dsh-local-link README · Mobile View：| Stock narrow-screen behavior | Mobile View in `1.2.x` |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop navigation competes with the conversation | Workspace and session navigation opens as a dismissible left drawer |
| Session metadata crowds the header | Context, model, access, preset, activity, and export move into a compact right drawer |
| Subagent details are difficult to scan or reach | On 0.1.5, a composer chip opens the catalog in a bottom sheet; on 0.1.7 and 0.2, Harness owns its header catalog and navigation |
| Hover-oriented session and workspace actions | Overflow actions remain visible and touch-accessible |
| Session changes can summon the software keyboard | Automatic composer focus is suppressed while intentional input focus still works |
| Desktop spacing ignores phone safe areas | Header, composer, tabs, media, overlays, and scrolling adapt to narrow viewports |

dsh-local-link README · Mobile View：These dark-theme previews were captured from real Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` browser sessions: mobile frames are `430 × 932`, desktop frames are `1440 × 1000`. The isolated profiles contain fictional workspaces, conversations, models, devices, and usage only. The Chinese README has its own Simplified Chinese captures; Russian documentation shares the English images. Subagents use the native Harness header catalog.
dsh-local-link README · Mobile View：| Navigation | Current session | Subagents | Conversation | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | | |

dsh-local-link README · Permissions：The remote browser inherits the selected Harness session's **Read only**, **Workspace write**, or **Full access** authority. Mobile View displays that value but does not create or weaken a permission layer. This applies to ordinary session operations; Settings, credentials, native Host actions, and agent-preset authoring remain loopback-only. Hiding `Add workspace` is a usability constraint, not an authorization boundary.

dsh-local-link README · Permissions：The responsive enhancements target viewports from 360 through 834 CSS pixels wide. The release matrix defines checks at `360 × 800`, `390 × 844`, `430 × 932`, and `768 × 1024`; release acceptance also requires portrait and landscape checks on a real phone. See [Mobile View](docs/MOBILE_VIEW.md) for behavior, theme persistence, compatibility surfaces, and the complete acceptance checklist.

dsh-local-link README · Manage trusted browsers：On the Harness computer, use `Paired devices` in the QR panel or open `Settings → Local access`. Each new browser starts as `My device`; its subtitle is detected automatically, for example `Phone · Chrome`, `Tablet · Safari`, or `Computer · Edge`.

dsh-local-link README · Manage trusted browsers：- `Rename` changes display metadata only.
- `Revoke` invalidates the browser credential and immediately closes its open Local Link WebSocket connections.
- A cleared cookie, private window, new browser profile, or revoked device needs a new invitation.

Browsers do not reliably distinguish laptops from desktop computers, so both are shown as `Computer`.

dsh-local-link README · Manage trusted browsers：Expand `Diagnostics` on the same Settings page to inspect the most recent local gateway events. `Copy report` produces issue-ready JSON and `Clear` removes the local history. The report contains event codes, timestamps, severity, and a small allowlisted context only; it never includes pairing tokens, cookies, IP addresses, device or session IDs, device names, request paths, prompts, conversations, or project files.

dsh-local-link README · Why it stays small：- **Stock Harness UI:** the plugin opens the existing Web client and live agent stream.
- **Local only:** one private-network gateway forwards to the loopback Harness Host.
- **Two runtime dependencies:** configuration schema support and QR generation.
- **No fingerprinting:** access is a random per-browser credential, not a device identity guess.
- **Native extension points:** sidebar and Settings content use Harness slots and locale services.
- **Native responsive enhancement:** the shipped Harness AppFrame stays mounted; registered conversation views and overlays remain dynamic.
- **JSON localization:** all visible plugin copy lives in matching locale dictionaries.
- **Local diagnostics:** a bounded, redacted event history helps debug installs without analytics or an external collector.

dsh-local-link README · How it works：```text
Desktop browser on 127.0.0.1:3080
  └─ Local access → one-use invitation
                         │
Phone / tablet / computer on the private LAN

The gateway does not create a second Harness session. During first connection it transfers the desktop browser's current session selection to the new browser origin; session data and ongoing conversation events still come from the same Host.
dsh-local-link README · How it works：Authorization uses a 256-bit random cookie credential. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. The editable name and detected device/browser text never grant access.

dsh-local-link README · How it works：The LAN authority is declared through Harness's official connection `trustedHosts` contract. This enables authenticated session API and WebSocket traffic without pretending that the phone is loopback. Harness `0.1.2-rc.1` and the verified `0.1.5` and `0.1.7` builds authenticate the transport as a whole, so Local Link itself rejects the configuration, credential, native Host-action, and agent-preset-authoring RPCs that earlier supported Harness builds kept loopback-only.

dsh-local-link README · Configuration：| Option | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listenHost` | `0.0.0.0` | Listen on local interfaces; request validation still accepts only private/loopback sources. |
| `listenPort` | `3088` | LAN gateway port. |
| `upstreamOrigin` | `http://127.0.0.1:3080` | Existing loopback Harness Web server. |
| `accessMode` | `pairing` | Require a one-use invitation and device cookie. |
| `pairingTtlSeconds` | `300` | Invitation lifetime. |
| `deviceTtlDays` | `90` | Remembered-browser lifetime. |
| `diagnosticsEnabled` | `true` | Keep the bounded local diagnostic history. |
| `diagnosticsMaxEntries` | `15` | Maximum retained events (`5`–`200`). |
| `diagnosticsFile` | next to `stateFile` | Local JSON event store; the bundled profile uses `~/.dsh/local-link/diagnostics.json`. |

dsh-local-link README · Configuration：`listenHost` accepts only `0.0.0.0` or an explicit private/loopback IP literal. Public listener addresses are rejected during startup; this configuration guard complements, rather than replaces, the operating-system firewall.

`trusted-lan` disables per-device authorization and should be reserved for isolated development networks. `pairing` is the supported default because a connected Harness browser can read files, submit prompts, approve actions, and trigger commands.

dsh-local-link README · Configuration：The plugin never creates firewall rules. If Windows prompts for network access, allow only the **Private** network profile and never forward port `3088` on the router.

dsh-local-link README · Troubleshooting and diagnostics：Diagnostics are a local, event-driven history of failures—not a request log. The plugin retains 15 events by default, shows the newest 12, coalesces identical five-second bursts, and records nothing for successful starts, requests, pairing, copies, renames, or revocations.

For support:

dsh-local-link README · Troubleshooting and diagnostics：1. Reproduce the failed action once.
2. Open `Settings → Local access → Diagnostics`.
3. Click `Refresh` if the panel was already open.
4. Use the newest stable event code to identify the failed boundary.
5. Click `Copy report`, review the JSON, and attach it to an issue if needed.

dsh-local-link README · Troubleshooting and diagnostics：The report never includes secrets, addresses, IDs, names, URLs, paths, prompts, conversations, or project data and is never uploaded automatically. See the [event reference and first checks](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md) for every tracked failure.

dsh-local-link README · Localization：Harness's active language selects the plugin dictionary; the plugin has no separate language switch.

The minimal automatic pairing page loads before Harness locale services are available. It reuses the same dictionaries and selects English or Chinese from the connecting browser's language list; English is the fallback.

| Language | Dictionary | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English | `src/locales/en.json` | Included |
| Chinese | `src/locales/zh.json` | Included |

dsh-local-link README · Localization：Dictionary keys are checked for parity in tests. To add a locale, copy `en.json`, translate values without changing keys, register the locale ID in `src/client.tsx`, extend the pre-client pairing-page language map in `src/gateway/pair-page.ts`, and run `npm test`.

dsh-local-link README · Known limitations：- LAN traffic is not encrypted; the current gateway uses plain HTTP.
- Revocation blocks new requests and reconnects and terminates every open Local Link WebSocket authenticated by the revoked device.
- A light/dark choice made from a remote browser is page-scoped in the supported Harness builds; reload returns to the Host preference and resolves `system` against the remote device.
- Invitations use the highest-ranked private IPv4 interface detected at startup; choosing among multiple LAN interfaces is not exposed yet.
- The shortcut that opens a specific Settings section uses a small semantic compatibility bridge because Harness does not expose a general settings-navigation service.
- Harness's footer-action container needs a compatibility layout rule when the full-width Cordis action is present.
- Mobile View targets viewports from 360 CSS pixels wide, but third-party fixed-width views, virtual keyboards, orientation changes, split-screen browsers, and operating-system text scaling still require real-device acceptance.
